records.name: React UAutoComplete
records.purpose: Controlled text input with consumer-supplied suggestions, debounced completeMethod, a suggestion overlay and keyboard navigation.
records.surface: UAutoCompleteProps is the exported props interface. UAutoComplete is generic over T (UAutoCompleteProps<T>) and is controlled for its value: value:T|null and onChange:(T|null)=>void are required; the visible text is local inputValue state, initialised from getOptionLabel(value) and re-synchronised by a useEffect on [value, getOptionLabel], so a parent re-render that passes a new optionLabel function identity re-sets the text to the label of value and discards in-progress typing. Other props: suggestions (default []), optionLabel (string key or function), minLength (1), delay (300), placeholder, disabled, fluid, loading, emptyMessage ('No results found'), showEmptyMessage (true), className, inputId, aria-label, completeMethod(UAutoCompleteCompleteEvent {originalEvent, query}), onSelect(UAutoCompleteSelectEvent {originalEvent, value}), onFocus, onBlur and onClear. The consumer owns the search: after delay ms the component calls completeMethod and shows the overlay; it never filters suggestions itself. Typing an empty string calls onChange(null) then onClear and hides the overlay; typing a non-empty string never calls onChange, so value only changes on selection. A query shorter than minLength hides the overlay. The debounce timer is stored in the searchTimeout ref, cleared only at the start of the next input event and never cleared on selection, blur or unmount, so a pending timer still calls completeMethod and sets overlayVisible after an option was chosen or after blur. Keyboard (event.code on the input): disabled preventDefaults every key; ArrowDown and ArrowUp move focusedIndex with wrap-around only while the overlay is visible; ArrowDown with an empty suggestions list sets focusedIndex to 0, and Enter then calls selectOption(event, suggestions[focusedIndex]) with undefined, which emits onChange(undefined) and onSelect with an undefined value; Enter or NumpadEnter with no focused item only preventDefaults; Escape hides the overlay. onMouseEnter sets focusedIndex with no mouse-leave reset. Accessibility: the input has role=combobox, aria-autocomplete=list, aria-expanded, aria-activedescendant (ids built from React.useId, which is used only by this component and select among the five) and an optional aria-label; the list gets id idRef_list but no aria-controls references it, there is no aria-haspopup, and the loader span is aria-hidden. The empty message li has role=option. aria-selected and the selected class use strict equality (option === value), so object suggestions match only by identity. onBlur always calls hide() before onBlur, so the overlay closes whenever the input loses focus; whether a mouse option click still fires after that blur was not executed. The overlay is an absolutely positioned div, no Portal. autoCompleteStyleModule defines classes root (filled, disabled, fluid), input, loader, overlay, list, option (focused, selected) and emptyMessage; AutoCompleteClassesParams (filled, disabled, fluid, focused, selected) is exported from the style file but not from the index barrel, and u-autocomplete-disabled and u-autocomplete-filled have no CSS rule, so they carry no styling. componentName autocomplete matches the Aura registry key autocomplete. Here option click does not check disabled: selectOption never reads the disabled prop, so an already-open overlay still selects after disabled becomes true. It is a plain function component, not a forwardRef: no ref, createPortal, useImperativeHandle, document listener, aria-controls or virtualization (no Scroller) is used. useComponentBase from @ultimate/react-core resolves cx classes and delegates style registration; those hooks are external foundation records, not duplicated here. The style module is hand-authored CSS registered through the base hook; no scoped style module imports @ultimate/uix-styles. List items use the array index as React key. Public runtime and types are named exports from both @ultimate/react and @ultimate/react/autocomplete; the root barrel line and manifest subpath are both present, and the manifest advertises dist entry/type paths, which does not prove a built or published package.

records.name: React UCascadeSelect
records.purpose: Controlled single-value dropdown over a nested option tree, drilling into groups to select a leaf.
records.surface: UCascadeSelectProps is the exported props interface. UCascadeSelect is generic over T and is controlled for its value: value:T|null and onChange:(T|null)=>void are required; options is unknown[], and optionLabel, optionValue and optionDisabled accept a string key or function. optionGroupChildren (default 'items') names the property holding child options. Other props: placeholder, disabled, emptyMessage, className, onSelect (UCascadeSelectChangeEvent {originalEvent, value}), onFocus and onBlur. There is no fluid, filter, showClear, onClear, inputId or aria-label prop. buildTree turns options into ProcessedOption nodes {option, key, parentKey, children} with index-path keys; a node with a non-empty children array is a group and every other node, including one with an empty array, is a leaf. findPathToValue matches only leaf nodes (getOptionValue(leaf) === value), so a value equal to a group never resolves a label; the label falls back to the placeholder. Clicking an enabled leaf calls onChange(optionValue) then onSelect and hides the overlay (clearing activeOptionPath); clicking a group drills in and emits nothing. optionDisabled blocks both selection and drilling. show() pre-expands the ancestors of the selected leaf. The drill state is the activeOptionPath key array. Toggling an open group removes it and its descendant keys; opening a group runs path.filter(key => key !== node.parentKey) before appending node.key, which removes the group's own parent key, so for a nested group the parent drops out of activeOptionPath and its sublist (containing the newly opened group) is no longer rendered, while top-level sibling groups are not collapsed. Read from source, not executed. Accessibility: the trigger is a span role=combobox with aria-haspopup=tree, aria-expanded and aria-disabled; the overlay list is role=tree (sublists too) with li role=treeitem, aria-selected (set on every item, true only for a selected leaf) and aria-expanded (groups only); the empty message is a treeitem rendered only when the top-level options array is empty, since sublists render only for non-empty groups. Keyboard on the trigger: Enter, NumpadEnter, Space and ArrowDown open (only when closed); Escape hides when open. There is no keyboard navigation inside the tree (no ArrowUp, ArrowRight or ArrowLeft handling and no option focus), no Tab handling, and the focused class is never passed, so u-cascade-select-option-content-focused (which has a CSS rule) is never emitted. The overlay stays open when disabled becomes true, option click does not check disabled (only optionDisabled blocks), and there is no outside-click or blur handler, so it closes only on leaf selection, Escape or a trigger click. Sublists are absolutely positioned relative to their parent li (inline style position:relative), no Portal. cascadeSelectStyleModule defines classes root (disabled, overlayVisible), label (placeholder), dropdown, overlay, list, sublist, option, optionContent (focused, selected, disabled), groupIcon and emptyMessage, each with a CSS rule; CascadeSelectClassesParams is exported from the style file but not from the index barrel. componentName cascade-select differs from the Aura registry key cascadeselect (registry value cascadeSelect). It is a plain function component, not a forwardRef: no ref, createPortal, useImperativeHandle, document listener, aria-controls or virtualization (no Scroller) is used. useComponentBase from @ultimate/react-core resolves cx classes and delegates style registration; those hooks are external foundation records, not duplicated here. The style module is hand-authored CSS registered through the base hook; no scoped style module imports @ultimate/uix-styles. List items use the array index as React key. Public runtime and types are named exports from both @ultimate/react and @ultimate/react/cascade-select; the root barrel line and manifest subpath are both present, and the manifest advertises dist entry/type paths, which does not prove a built or published package.

records.name: React UListbox
records.purpose: Controlled always-visible option list with single or multiple selection and an optional filter.
records.surface: UListboxProps is the exported props interface. UListbox is generic over T and is controlled for its value: value:T|T[]|null and onChange:(T|T[]|null)=>void are required; options, optionLabel, optionValue and optionDisabled work as in select. Other props: multiple (false), filter, filterPlaceholder, disabled, emptyMessage, className, aria-label, onSelectionChange (UListboxChangeEvent {originalEvent, value:T|T[]}), onFocus and onBlur, which are attached to the ul and not the root. There is no inputId, fluid or onClear. It is not overlay-based: the filter header (searchbox) and the list render inline. Selecting an enabled option calls onChange then onSelectionChange. In single mode (multiple false) it emits the option value, so clicking the selected option again re-emits the same value and onChange never emits null; in multiple mode it emits a new array (a non-array value counts as []), which can be empty when the last item is deselected. isSelected uses strict equality in single mode and Array.includes in multiple mode; multiple renders a read-only, tabIndex -1 checkbox per option. Accessibility: the ul is role=listbox with aria-multiselectable={multiple} (rendered as false in single mode), optional aria-label and tabIndex 0 (-1 when disabled); options are role=option with aria-selected and aria-disabled; the empty message li has role=option. There are no option ids and no aria-activedescendant, so the focused option is conveyed only by the focused class. Keyboard on the ul (event.code): ArrowDown and ArrowUp move focus, Home and End set 0 and length-1 (End on an empty list gives -1 and Home ignores disabled options), Enter, NumpadEnter and Space select the focused option. disabled blocks the keyboard handler and sets tabIndex -1, but the filter input stays enabled and option click does not check disabled, so clicks still emit while disabled; only optionDisabled blocks selection. moveFocus has a non-terminating loop edge case: its do/while stops early only when next equals the previous focusedIndex, so when focusedIndex is -1 and every visible option is disabled the loop never exits; from -1 ArrowUp lands on length-2. Read from source, not executed. listboxStyleModule defines classes root (disabled), header, filter, listContainer, list, option (focused, selected, disabled) and emptyMessage, each with a CSS rule; ListboxClassesParams is exported from the style file but not from the index barrel. componentName listbox matches the Aura registry key listbox. It is a plain function component, not a forwardRef: no ref, createPortal, useImperativeHandle, document listener, aria-controls or virtualization (no Scroller) is used. useComponentBase from @ultimate/react-core resolves cx classes and delegates style registration; those hooks are external foundation records, not duplicated here. The style module is hand-authored CSS registered through the base hook; no scoped style module imports @ultimate/uix-styles. List items use the array index as React key. Public runtime and types are named exports from both @ultimate/react and @ultimate/react/listbox; the root barrel line and manifest subpath are both present, and the manifest advertises dist entry/type paths, which does not prove a built or published package.

records.name: React UMultiSelect
records.purpose: Controlled array-valued dropdown with checkbox options, select-all, filter, clear and a summarised trigger label.
records.surface: UMultiSelectProps is the exported props interface. UMultiSelect is generic over T and is controlled for its value: value:T[] and onChange:(T[])=>void are required (a non-array value is treated as []); options, optionLabel, optionValue and optionDisabled work as in select. Other props: placeholder, disabled, fluid, filter, filterPlaceholder, showClear, showToggleAll (true), maxSelectedLabels (3), selectedItemsLabel ('{0} items selected'), emptyMessage, className, onSelectionChange (UMultiSelectChangeEvent {originalEvent, value:T[]}), onFocus, onBlur and onClear. There is no inputId, no aria-label prop, no onSelect and no aria-activedescendant or option ids. Toggling an option (click, or Enter, NumpadEnter or Space on the focused option) calls onChange(newArray) then onSelectionChange and does not close the overlay. toggleAll (the header 'Select All' checkbox, aria-label hard-coded in English) calls only onChange and never onSelectionChange; it acts on the visible, non-disabled options only. The clear icon calls onChange([]) then onClear and never onSelectionChange; it is an aria-hidden span reachable only by mouse. The trigger label is the placeholder when empty (the span is empty when there is no placeholder), the comma-joined option labels (String(v) for values without an option) up to maxSelectedLabels, and otherwise selectedItemsLabel with {0} replaced by the count. The trigger is a span role=combobox with aria-haspopup=listbox, aria-expanded and aria-disabled; the list is role=listbox with aria-multiselectable=true; the empty-message li has role=option; each option renders a read-only, tabIndex -1 checkbox. The header div is always rendered, even when showToggleAll and filter are both false. Keyboard on the trigger: ArrowDown and ArrowUp open, or move focus when open; Enter, NumpadEnter and Space open, or toggle the focused option when open; Escape hides when open; Tab hides. There is no Home or End handling, and the filter searchbox has no key handling. moveFocus has a non-terminating loop edge case: its do/while stops early only when next equals the previous focusedIndex, so when focusedIndex is -1 and every visible option is disabled the loop never exits; from -1 ArrowUp lands on length-2. Read from source, not executed. The overlay stays open when disabled becomes true and option click does not check disabled (only optionDisabled blocks toggling); there is no outside-click or blur handler, so the overlay closes only on Escape, Tab or a trigger click. The overlay is an absolutely positioned div, no Portal. multiSelectStyleModule defines classes root (disabled, overlayVisible, fluid), label (placeholder), dropdown, clearIcon, overlay, header, filter, listContainer, list, option (focused, selected, disabled) and emptyMessage, each with a CSS rule; MultiSelectClassesParams is exported from the style file but not from the index barrel. componentName multi-select differs from the Aura registry key multiselect (registry value multiSelect). It is a plain function component, not a forwardRef: no ref, createPortal, useImperativeHandle, document listener, aria-controls or virtualization (no Scroller) is used. useComponentBase from @ultimate/react-core resolves cx classes and delegates style registration; those hooks are external foundation records, not duplicated here. The style module is hand-authored CSS registered through the base hook; no scoped style module imports @ultimate/uix-styles. List items use the array index as React key. Public runtime and types are named exports from both @ultimate/react and @ultimate/react/multi-select; the root barrel line and manifest subpath are both present, and the manifest advertises dist entry/type paths, which does not prove a built or published package.

records.name: React USelect
records.purpose: Controlled single-value dropdown with option accessors, optional filter and clear, and an inline overlay panel.
records.surface: USelectProps is the exported props interface. USelect is generic over T and is controlled for its value: value:T|null and onChange:(T|null)=>void are required; options is unknown[] and optionLabel, optionValue and optionDisabled accept a string key or a function through the local resolve helper. Other props: placeholder, disabled, fluid, filter, filterPlaceholder, showClear, emptyMessage ('No results found'), className, inputId, aria-label, onSelect (USelectChangeEvent {originalEvent, value}), onFocus, onBlur and onClear. The selected option is found with strict equality (getOptionValue(option) === value); when none matches, the placeholder is shown and the placeholder class is set. Choosing an enabled option calls onChange(optionValue) then onSelect and hides the overlay; the clear icon (shown when showClear, value != null and not disabled) calls onChange(null) then onClear and never calls onSelect, and it is an aria-hidden span reachable only by mouse. Overlay, focusedIndex and filterValue are local state; hide() resets all three. The trigger is a span role=combobox with aria-haspopup=listbox, aria-expanded, aria-disabled, aria-activedescendant, tabIndex and aria-label={ariaLabel ?? label} (undefined when there is neither); inputId is applied as its id. The list has role=listbox and id idRef_list but nothing sets aria-controls; the empty-message li has role=option; the dropdown arrow div is role=button with aria-hidden. Keyboard on the trigger (event.code): ArrowDown and ArrowUp open, or move focus when open; Home and End set focusedIndex to 0 and length-1 only while open and Home ignores disabled options; Enter, NumpadEnter and Space open, or select the focused option when open; Escape hides when open; Tab hides. With filter, a searchbox input handles ArrowDown, ArrowUp, Enter, NumpadEnter and Escape only. moveFocus has a non-terminating loop edge case: its do/while advances until an enabled option is found and stops early only when next equals the previous focusedIndex, so when focusedIndex is -1 and every visible option is disabled the loop never exits. Also, from focusedIndex -1 ArrowUp lands on length-2 rather than the last item. Both were read from source, not executed. The overlay stays open when disabled becomes true (disabled gates only show, the trigger and dropdown click handlers and the trigger keydown), and option click does not check disabled: only optionDisabled blocks selection. There is no outside-click or blur handler, so the overlay closes only on selection, Escape, Tab or a trigger click. The filter input is not disabled when the select is. The overlay is an absolutely positioned div, no Portal. selectStyleModule defines classes root (disabled, overlayVisible, fluid), label (placeholder), dropdown, clearIcon, overlay, header, filter, listContainer, list, option (focused, selected, disabled) and emptyMessage, each with a CSS rule; SelectClassesParams (including selected and focused, which root and label ignore) is exported from the style file but not from the index barrel. componentName select matches the Aura registry key select. It is a plain function component, not a forwardRef: no ref, createPortal, useImperativeHandle, document listener, aria-controls or virtualization (no Scroller) is used. useComponentBase from @ultimate/react-core resolves cx classes and delegates style registration; those hooks are external foundation records, not duplicated here. The style module is hand-authored CSS registered through the base hook; no scoped style module imports @ultimate/uix-styles. List items use the array index as React key. Public runtime and types are named exports from both @ultimate/react and @ultimate/react/select; the root barrel line and manifest subpath are both present, and the manifest advertises dist entry/type paths, which does not prove a built or published package.
